'''''Origanum onites''''', the '''Cretan oregano''',{{citation needed|date=May 2016}} '''Greek oregano''',<ref name=GRIN>{{citation |url=https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?id=405610 |title=USDA GRIN Taxonomy |access-date=12 May 2016}}</ref> '''pot marjoram'''<ref name=GRIN/> or '''Ellinikí rίgani''' in Greek (Ελληνική ρίγανη), is a plant species in the genus ''[[Origanum]]'' found in [[Sicily]], [[Greece]] and [[Turkey]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Origanum onites (Lamiaceae) in Greece: Distribution, Volatile Oil Yield, and Composition|first1= D.|last1= Vokou|first2= S. |last2=Kokkini |first3= J-M. |last3=Bessière|journal= Economic Botany|year= 1988|volume=42|issue= 3| pages =407–412|jstor=4255090|doi=10.1007/BF02860163|s2cid= 41665057}}</ref> It has similar flavors as common [[oregano]]. It has antimicrobial activities.<ref>{{Cite journal|pmid=18800908|year=2008|last1=Sarac|first1=N|last2=Ugur|first2=A|title=Antimicrobial activities of the essential oils of Origanum onites L., Origanum vulgare L. Subspecies hirtum (Link) Ietswaart, Satureja thymbra L., and Thymus cilicicus Boiss. & Bal. Growing wild in Turkey|volume=11|issue=3|pages=568–73|doi=10.1089/jmf.2007.0520|journal=Journal of Medicinal Food}}</ref>

==Chemistry==
The plant contains the chemical compounds [[thymol]], [[carvacrol]] and [[cedrol]].{{citation needed|date=September 2016}}
